To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the salt-tolerant clone maintained a lower ion content and higher water content in all its organs than the salt-sensitive one, and this difference between the two clones was more pronounced for older leaves than for younger leaves or the stem.

in the more tolerant Agrostis st. the salt ions were more evenly distributed between the individual organs and the plants maintained viable water content, and in the more sensitive Agrostis st., salt ions were accumulated to a greater extent in the older leaves and the water content was reduced in the lower leaves.
salt tolerance of the clone is based on the ability to maintain viable water content in the lower parts of the shoot, while avoiding the accumulation of salt to toxic levels in the leaves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of salinity on the growth of a salt-tolerant and a salt-sensitive clone of Agrostism stolonifera.
the effects of NaCl treatment on the ion and water content in the individual leaves and stems of two clones of Agrostris stolonifers L., one tolerant and one sensitive to salt stress.
the effects of NaCl treatment on ion content and water status in different shoot organs of two clones of Agrostris stolonifero differing in their salt resistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in salt stress, the salt-sensitive plants dehydrated and accumulated ions in older leaves, while the more tolerant ones did not dehydrate and accumulated ions to a lesser degree.
the salt-tolerant clone was able to maintain a lower Na+ and Cl- content, a higher K+/Na+ ratio and a viable water status in all organs during and following NaCl treatment.

the salt-tolerant plants were more efficient in maintaining their water balance, while the salt-sensitive plants were more efficient than their salt-tolerant counterparts in excluding Na+ and Cl- from the younger leaves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the salt-tolerant clone of Agrostistolonifera maintained a higher K+/Na+ ratio, and a lower Na+ content, in all organs, and that the sensitive clone suffered from a greater degree of dehydration.
, for both clones, the salt tolerance is based on the ability of the plant to maintain a high K+ concentration and to prevent the loss of water.
in the salt-sensitive clone, Na+ and CI− accumulated in the older leaves and the water content of the youngest leaves decreased to a greater degree than in the resistant clone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is necessary to consider the individual organs when studying salt tolerance in Agrostis stonolifera.
the analysis of individual organs and of whole shoots gives different information, and that the analysis on several bases gives additional information on the physiological processes involved.

, in addition to the well known whole shoot analysis, the organ-by-organ approach is also valuable for revealing the differences in ion and osmotic adjustment between plants of different salt resistance.
